evidenceAudit.scope: Pregnant women at low risk: booking, risk stratification, routine tests, scheduled reviews, supplements and referral triggers. Verified against the Saudi MOH Pocket Manual in Obstetrics & Gynaecology (antenatal care chapter) and NICE NG201 (antenatal care), with NG133 (hypertension) and NG3 (gestational diabetes) for referral thresholds.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: MOH manual (2014) not updated to NG201 schedule

pathophysiology.summary: Routine antenatal care aims to confirm gestation, detect conditions that threaten mother or baby (anaemia, hypertensive disorders, diabetes, infection, fetal growth problems, malpresentation) early, and prepare for birth and feeding. Most women remain low risk; risk is reassessed at each contact.
keyMechanisms: Pregnancy increases plasma volume more than red-cell mass (haemodilution) and iron demand — the reason for serial haemoglobin checks and iron (MOH).
Placental hormones increase insulin resistance from the second trimester — the window for GDM screening at 24–28 weeks.
Abnormal placentation can present later as hypertension, proteinuria or growth restriction — hence BP, urine and fundal-height checks at every visit.
Early ultrasound dates the pregnancy more accurately than the last menstrual period (MOH).

symptoms: Usually none; ask about bleeding, pain, fluid loss, headache, visual change, reduced fetal movements at every visit (MOH records fetal movements).
Mood, domestic abuse, smoking and medicines at booking (NICE NG201).
physicalSigns: BP (sitting); weight and BMI; urine dipstick (protein, ketones, sugar) at every visit (MOH).
Symphysis–fundal height within ±3 cm of gestation in weeks from 26–36 weeks (MOH); presentation documented.
redFlags: BP 140/90 mmHg or more after 20 weeks — refer within 24 h; 160/110 or more — same day (NICE NG201)
Vaginal bleeding, severe headache, visual disturbance, epigastric pain
Reduced fetal movements after 24+0 weeks — contact maternity services immediately (NICE)
Fundal height small or large for dates — growth scan

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Previous complications, medical disease, multiple pregnancy — consultant-led care (MOH).
New hypertension after 20 weeks with proteinuria or organ dysfunction.

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Hb below 10 g/dL: repeat monthly; below 9 g/dL: check ferritin (MOH).
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Iron twice daily if Hb below 10 g/dL (MOH).

clinicalManagement.title: Booking
actions: History and examination; classify low or high risk — high risk seen by a consultant (MOH).
Calculate EDD by LMP and confirm with early ultrasound (MOH).
Booking bloods and urine as above; assess VTE, GDM and pre-eclampsia risk (NICE NG201).
Aspirin for women at risk of pre-eclampsia per NICE NG133 (see Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy topic).

clinicalManagement.title: Scheduled visits
actions: Low-risk women may be followed in primary care up to 36 weeks (MOH).
NICE plans 10 appointments for nulliparous and 7 for parous women.
Every visit: fetal movements, complaints, BP, weight, urine dipstick; fundal height 26–36 weeks; presentation; palpation for breech after 36 weeks (NICE).
CBC at 28 and 36 weeks; GDM screening at 24–28 weeks.

clinicalManagement.title: Supplements
actions: Folic acid 1 mg daily for the first 3 months (MOH).
Iron: ferrous fumarate 200 mg or ferrous sulfate 60 mg once daily if Hb above 10 g/dL, twice daily if below 10 g/dL (MOH).

clinicalManagement.title: Education and referral
actions: Physiological changes, birth preparation, breastfeeding, nutrition; genetic counselling for family history, previous affected child or recurrent miscarriage (MOH).
Contact maternity services immediately for reduced fetal movements after 24+0 weeks (NICE).
Refer for hypertension, abnormal glucose, anaemia below 9 g/dL, abnormal growth or presentation.

learningObjectives: Provide structured routine antenatal care and recognise when to escalate.
